intro: Hobbies, family customs, cooking together and a few words for thinking aloud.
p.afición.consejo: It ends in -ción, so the stress is at the end. Someone who has one is an «aficionado».
p.costumbre.consejo: You say «tener la costumbre de» + infinitive, or «por costumbre».
p.tradición.consejo: It ends in -ción: the stress is at the end. A tradition passes from family to family.
p.receta.consejo: It is also the doctor's paper for buying medicines.
p.sartén.consejo: It is feminine: «la sartén». It has an accent because it ends in n and the stress is at the end.
p.agua.consejo: It is feminine but takes «el» in the singular: «el agua fría». In plural, «las aguas».
p.probar.consejo: The o becomes ue: «pruebo». You taste food and also try on clothes.
p.sobremesa.glosa: time at the table after a meal
p.sobremesa.consejo: It is a very Spanish word: people chat, laugh and nobody is in a hurry.
p.recuerdo.consejo: It is also an object you bring back from a trip. «Recuerdos a tu familia» is a greeting.
p.soñar con.consejo: The o becomes ue: «sueño con». It takes «con»: «sueño con viajar».
p.reflexionar sobre.consejo: You say «reflexionar sobre» or «reflexionar acerca de» a topic.
p.convencido.consejo: It takes «de»: «convencido de que…». Feminine: «convencida». It comes from «convencer».
p.curioso.consejo: It can be a person («es curioso») or a fact («un dato curioso»). Feminine: «curiosa».
b1.texto:
**Hobbies and customs.** The **afición** is what you do for pleasure. The **costumbre** is what you do often and the **tradición** passes from family to family. You say **tener la costumbre de** + infinitive.

**Cooking together.** The **receta**, the ingredients, the **sartén**, the rice, the stock. You **remueves** the rice, **pruebas** the stock and add salt. The **sobremesa** is the time you stay at the table after eating.

**Giving opinions.** **Creo que…**, **estoy convencido de que…** (with indicative) and **dudo que…**, **no creo que…** (with subjunctive). You can **soñar con** something and **reflexionar sobre** a topic.

**Thinking.** The **recuerdo** is what you keep of the past; «compañía» is the people you are with; «razón» is the reason for something.

**Two meanings.** **Probar** is to taste and also to try.
b2.f0.texto: Do you have your grandmother's paella recipe?
b2.f1.texto: It is not written down anywhere.
b2.f2.texto: Then you stir the rice while I heat the pan.
b2.f3.texto: It smells like the kitchen of my childhood.
b2.f4.texto: Do you want to taste the stock before adding the salt?
b2.f5.texto: Only a little water is missing.
b2.f6.texto: I am convinced the after-lunch chat will be the best part of the day.
b2.f7.texto: Cooking together is a good custom of this neighbourhood.
b4.texto:
When you **assert** an opinion, the following verb is **indicative**: **Creo que**, **estoy convencido de que**, **me parece que** + indicative.

When you **doubt** or **deny**, it is **subjunctive**: **Dudo que**, **no creo que**, **no me parece que** + subjunctive.

- **Estoy convencido de que** la receta es buena.
- **Dudo que** la paella salga bien a la primera.
- **No creo que** sea una receta difícil.
b4.e0.texto: I am convinced the recipe is good.
b4.e1.texto: I doubt the paella will turn out well the first time.
b4.e2.texto: I do not think it is a difficult recipe.
b5.f0.texto: In the neighbourhood park, the improvised kitchens have been steaming since noon.
b5.f1.texto: Over the fire, enormous pans crackle with a smell of oil and saffron.
b5.f2.texto: The cooks slowly stir the rice with big wooden paddles.
b5.f3.texto: Some wear the same apron their grandfather used.
b5.f4.texto: The smoke rises among the trees and mingles with the children's laughter.
b5.f5.texto: When the rice is ready, everyone sits at long tables under the plane trees.
b5.f6.texto: Nobody is in a hurry to leave the table.
b5.f7.texto: The voices blend with the noise of plates and the clinking of glasses.
b5.f8.texto: An old woman tells an ancient memory to the youngest.
b5.f9.texto: As evening falls, the park falls silent and smells of dead wood fires.
b6.o0.refuerzo: The kitchen table is furniture, not a moment.
b6.o1: el rato en la mesa después de comer
b6.o1.refuerzo: Yes: it is the chatting time after the meal.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Dessert is a dish; the sobremesa is the time after.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: before a stressed a the singular article is «el»: el agua.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is normal for feminine nouns, but «agua» takes «el» in the singular.
b7.pregunta: Which article goes with «agua» in the singular?
b8.frase: Cocinar juntos es una buena costumbre
b8.traduccion: Cooking together is a good custom
b9.o0.refuerzo: Heating raises the temperature; it is not tasting.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Serving is putting the soup in bowls.
b9.o2: tomar un poco para ver a qué sabe
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «probar» is taking a little to know the taste.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: after doubting the subjunctive is used: «salga».
b11.o1.refuerzo: The indicative is used to assert, not to doubt.
b11.o2.refuerzo: The future is not used after «dudo que» either.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «remover» is moving food with a spoon or paddle.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Buying has nothing to do with stirring.
b12.pregunta: What does someone who stirs the rice do?
p.paella.consejo: The ll sounds like «y». Feminine: «la paella».
p.escrita.consejo: Feminine participle. It agrees with a feminine noun.
p.caldo.consejo: Masculine: «el caldo». The c before a sounds like «k».
p.convencida.consejo: Feminine of «convencido». The v sounds like «b».
p.difícil.consejo: Tilde on the i marks the stress: di-FI-thil.
p.cocinas.consejo: Feminine plural: «la cocina». The c before i sounds like «th».
p.humean.consejo: The h is silent. Compare «humea», the singular.
p.enormes.consejo: Plural of «enorme», which has the same form for masculine and feminine.
p.crepitan.consejo: The sound of hot oil. The stress is on PI.
p.azafrán.consejo: The z sounds like «th» in Spain. Stress on the last syllable.
p.usaba.consejo: The -aba ending is the past for habit: «usaba» means «used to».
p.mezclan.consejo: The z before cl sounds like «th» in Spain: mez-KLAN.
p.vasos.consejo: The v sounds like «b»: BA-sos. Masculine: «el vaso».
p.leña.consejo: The ñ sounds like «ny»: LE-nya. Feminine: «la leña».
